sections.description: Bliss defines Power Core as the core driver within a company that shapes how it serves customers and transforms the organization.
sections.title: Power Core concept introduced

sections.description: In auto, the traditional Power Core has been marketing—brochures and events—that promises a customer experience, which the actual dealership experience may fail to fulfill.
sections.title: Industry example: automotive power core and dealership experience

sections.description: In financial services, Power Core tends to center on internal tasks (sales or actuarial/claims work) rather than directly serving customers, with rewards tied to those outputs rather than customer value.
sections.title: Industry example: financial services power core

sections.description: Bliss advocates first identifying the Power Core inside a company and then taking initial actions that align the organization with desired customer transformation.
sections.title: Approach: identify and align with your Power Core

sections.description: She cites Microsoft’s contextual help prompts as an example of a product-based Power Core that centers improvements around the product to gain traction.
sections.title: Microsoft example: product-based power core

sections.description: Bliss contrasts her early career approach with a more energetic, customer-centric stance and introduces two actions: engage the Power Core and secure early traction to justify broader change.
sections.title: Execution: energize with passion and engage the Power Core

summary: Jeanne Bliss introduces the concept of a Power Core—an internal organizational focus that drives how a company delivers value to customers. Using industry examples (automotive marketing, financial services, and a Microsoft service-model reference), she explains that a Power Core often governs rewards and behavior, sometimes detached from real customer outcomes. The talk then outlines a practical path: identify your Power Core, align actions with it to drive customer transformation, and begin with early traction—often by improving the core product or service—before expanding to broader initiatives. A notable example is Microsoft’s pop-up help as a product-based Power Core, and Bliss emphasizes energizing leadership with passion to engage the Power Core and earn the right to scale change.
title: Power Core: Identifying and Leveraging Your Company's Customer-Centric Core
